labels.text: Code: Sign In to AGI Cloud

S3.01.needs: a browser and an AGI account (or a way to create one)
S3.01.note: The browser handoff lives in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/account-auth/deviceAuth.ts; the quoted line in the plan was not found, but the sign-in command and device flow are present.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Sign In to AGI Cloud" and press Enter.
Finish the approval in the browser page that opens, then return to VS Code.
Look at the AGI panel: the signed-in account state should show, as Expected says.
S3.01.where: Command Palette > Code: Sign In to AGI Cloud (also the Sign in button in the Settings panel)

labels.text: Code: Sign In to AGI Cloud

S3.02.needs: a browser and an email address or a supported provider account; not signed in to AGI Cloud
S3.02.note: The sign-up link is in apps/web/app/auth/device/page.tsx, linked to /signup; the page's condition for showing the link was not traced, so the tester should confirm it appears while signed out.
steps: Sign out of AGI Cloud in VS Code if signed in, then press Cmd+Shift+P and run "Code: Sign In to AGI Cloud".
In the browser page that opens, look for the "Create account" link beside the sign-in link.
Click "Create account" and check that a sign-up page opens, as Expected says.
S3.02.where: Command Palette > Code: Sign In to AGI Cloud, then the browser page > Create account

labels.text: Code: Turn Memory On or Off

S3.25.note: The walkthrough step explains memory; the choice is changed through the Memory commands, not a setup screen that asks at first run. The plan's Code line pointed at package.json:878, which holds that step.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Memory" and press Enter.
Read the memory choice shown, then run "Code: Turn Memory On or Off" from the palette to choose whether memory is used.
Run "Code: Turn Memory On or Off" again to change the choice and check the memory state changes, as Expected says.
S3.25.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory (or Get started with AGI Code walkthrough > Decide what AGI remembers > Open Memory)

S3.31.needs: a phone with the AGI Mobile app, and an AGI account signed in on both
S3.31.note: The account binding is set in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/remote-control/remoteControlService.ts, which the tester cannot see; the phone-side wording 'Pair with Desktop' comes from vscode.json remote.howToPair, not verified in the mobile app.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Remote Control" and press Enter.
In the panel titled "Remote Control", click "Pair a phone".
On the phone, open the AGI Mobile app and pair with the desktop by scanning the Pairing QR code shown (or typing the pairing code).
Check the panel changes to connected for that phone, and that the pairing code expires in a few minutes, as Expected says.
S3.31.where: Command Palette > Code: Remote Control, then the Pair a phone button

S3.35.note: The code that runs after the last step (completeOnboarding in ChatStateManager) was not traced to confirm it opens a chat; the first-run screen shows automatically only when it has not been seen before.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Show Getting Started" and press Enter.
Read the first screen "Work with your code", then click Next to move through the steps.
On the last step click the button shown there ("Open chat" with no runtime, otherwise "Done").
Check that you land on a first chat, as Expected says.
S3.35.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Getting Started (first-run setup screen in the AGI sidebar)

S3.36.note: The walkthrough's saved progress is VS Code's own walkthrough state, not code in the extension, and the first-run screen step index is not saved (only the seen flag is), so resuming there is unverified. Opening the walkthrough from the Welcome page was not traced in the code.
steps: Open the walkthrough "Get started with AGI Code" from VS Code's Welcome or Get Started page.
Complete one step, such as "Decide what AGI remembers" by clicking its Open Memory link, then close VS Code.
Reopen VS Code and the walkthrough, and check the completed step is still ticked, as Expected says.
Optionally, run "Code: Show Getting Started" and click Next once, then close and reopen the window to see whether the screen restarts at its first step.
S3.36.where: Get started with AGI Code (VS Code walkthrough), and Code: Show Getting Started for the first-run steps

labels.text: Sign in for AGI subscription features. Local and provider BYOK do not require an AGI plan.
Sign in or add a provider key

S3.37.needs: a Free account or no account
S3.37.note: Searched apps/extension-vscode/src for guest, sign-up, and carry-over wording and found no guest mode or guest-to-account conversion. Only partial evidence: without sign-in, Local and provider BYOK models are shown as usable ('On this device'), and locked cloud models ask for a sign-in or provider key.
